title: Ἀνὴρ πηρός
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 54 (= Perry 37). Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ἀνὴρ πηρὸς εἰώθει πᾶν τὸ ἐπιτιθέμενον εἰς τὰς αὐτοῦ χεῖρας ζῷον ἐφαπτόμενος λέγειν ὁποῖόν τί ἐστι.
sentences.tr: Anēr pēros eiōthei pan to epitithemenon eis tas autou cheiras zōion ephaptomenos legein hopoion ti esti.
sentences.l: A disabled man was accustomed, touching every animal placed into his hands, to say what sort of thing it was.
sentences.i: A blind man had the habit of handling any animal put into his hands and saying what kind it was.
sentences.n: πηρός is 'maimed, disabled'; the fable's own detail — he judges by touch alone — shows that the disability meant here is blindness. εἰώθει is a pluperfect used as a plain past, 'he was in the habit'. The article with a participle, τὸ ἐπιτιθέμενον … ζῷον, makes 'the animal that was being put'.

sentences.t: Καὶ δή ποτε λυκιδίου αὐτῷ ἐπιδοθέντος, ψηλαφήσας καὶ ἀμφιγνοῶν εἶπεν· « Οὐκ οἶδα πότερον λύκου ἐστὶν ἢ ἀλώπεκος ἢ τοιούτου τινὸς ζῴου γέννημα· τοῦτο μέντοι σαφῶς ἐπίσταμαι ὅτι οὐκ ἐπιτήδειον τοῦτο τὸ ζῷον προβάτων ποίμνῃ συνιέναι. »
sentences.tr: Kai dē pote lykidiou autōi epidothentos, psēlaphēsas kai amphignoōn eipen· « Ouk oida poteron lykou estin ē alōpekos ē toioutou tinos zōiou gennēma· touto mentoi saphōs epistamai hoti ouk epitēdeion touto to zōion probatōn poimnēi synienai. »
sentences.l: And one day, a wolf cub having been handed to him, having felt it over and being in doubt, he said: « I do not know whether it is the offspring of a wolf or of a fox or of some such animal; this, however, I know clearly, that this animal is not fit to go along with a flock of sheep. »
sentences.i: One day a wolf cub was handed to him; he felt it over, and being unsure, said: « I cannot tell whether this is the young of a wolf or a fox or some such creature; but this much I know for certain — it is not fit to go about with a flock of sheep. »
sentences.n: λυκίδιον is a diminutive, 'little wolf', a cub; the -ίδιον ending is the ordinary way of making one. Another genitive absolute brings in the new circumstance. πότερον … ἤ … ἤ opens an indirect question with three branches, though πότερον strictly asks 'which of two'. συνιέναι here is from σύνειμι (εἶμι, 'go'), 'to go along with', not from συνίημι.

sentences.t: Οὕτω τῶν πονηρῶν ἡ διάθεσις πολλάκις καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ σώματος καταφαίνεται.
sentences.tr: Houtō tōn ponērōn hē diathesis pollakis kai apo tou sōmatos kataphainetai.
sentences.l: So the disposition of the wicked often shows itself even from the body.
sentences.n: Οὕτω standing alone as the closing hinge, of the same family as οὕτω καί, 'so too'. διάθεσις is the settled cast of character; καί before ἀπὸ τοῦ σώματος is 'even'.
